feature: UI "hello world" — proves a headless build agent can trigger + read back a real UI test result end to end
notes: Part of Epic #803, UI sibling of #957's hello-world-sql.json. Purpose is NOT to test
deep product logic — it proves the #898 remote-trigger-over-HTTP pipeline (headless POST
/admin/deploy/test-run -> BuildConsole claims + runs uiSteps via a live WebView2 ->
POST .../complete -> headless GET .../<runId> poll) can drive a real browser and read back
a genuine pass/fail, so more complex uiSteps manifests can be trusted.
Content assertions reuse #892's containsAny/containsNone. The framework has no DOM-text
assertion (uiStep `expect` only checks element state: visible/hidden/present/absent —
textContains is silently ignored, see test-manifests/copilot-readiness/money-path-e2e.json's unused
'ready' textContains), so containsAny/containsNone run against a captureResponse'd API
call the homepage genuinely makes on load, not raw rendered DOM text. Step 1 re-navigates
to '/' (RunAsync's own initial navigation to baseUrl happens before any uiStep's
captureResponse is armed, so it would miss the fetch) to capture
artifacts/api-server/src/routes/public-hero.ts's GET /api/public/hero-headlines, which
artifacts/shane-mccaw-consulting/src/hooks/useHeroHeadlines.ts's useTypewriterHeadline()
fetches unconditionally on mount to hydrate Home.tsx's hero headline.
jsonPath $[0].leadText scopes containsAny/containsNone to that one field's string value
(server always orders by sort_order ASC, so index 0 is deterministic) rather than the raw
response body — the response also carries a legitimate seasonalLabel:null for evergreen
rows (see lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-07-19-hero-headlines.sql), so a containsNone check
for the literal word 'null' against the WHOLE body would false-fail on that legitimate field.
containsAny lists all 3 seed-migration headlines' lead_text (2026-07-19-hero-headlines.sql,
matching useHeroHeadlines.ts's own FALLBACK_HEADLINE for row 1) so the assertion survives
any one of the three being reordered — but Shane's admin-panel Hero Headlines screen lets
these be edited at runtime, so if all three seeded headlines have since been replaced this
assertion will legitimately fail and should be refreshed against whatever real copy is live.
Second step asserts the header CTA button (a stable, code-literal element, not DB content)
is genuinely visible after load — the structural 'did it load' half of the hello-world proof.
